decision.summary: The Federal Reserve lowered the federal funds rate by 25 basis points to a target range of 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent.

changes.quote: Since earlier in the year, labor market conditions have generally eased, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low.
changes.explanation: The Fed updated its description of the job market to reflect that labor conditions have eased over the year while joblessness remains low.

changes.quote: Inflation has made progress toward the Committee's 2 percent objective but remains somewhat elevated.
changes.explanation: The Fed removed the word "further" regarding inflation progress, signaling an ongoing approach without overstating the latest step.

changes.quote: The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.
changes.explanation: The Fed removed language about having greater confidence in sustainably reaching 2 percent inflation, keeping its risk assessment balanced.

changes.quote: In support of its goals, the Committee decided to lower the target range for the federal funds rate by 1/4 percentage point to 4-1/2 to 4-3/4 percent.
changes.explanation: The Fed opted for a smaller 25 basis point rate cut this time compared to the previous 50 basis point reduction.

changes.quote: Voting for the monetary policy action were Jerome H. Powell, Chair; John C. Williams, Vice Chair; Thomas I. Barkin; Michael S. Barr; Raphael W. Bostic; Michelle W. Bowman; Lisa D. Cook; Mary C. Daly; Beth M. Hammack; Philip N. Jefferson; Adriana D. Kugler; and Christopher J. Waller.
changes.explanation: The decision was unanimous with no dissenters, unlike the previous meeting.

tone_quotes.quote: Recent indicators suggest that economic activity has continued to expand at a solid pace.
Since earlier in the year, labor market conditions have generally eased, and the unemployment rate has moved up but remains low.
The Committee judges that the risks to achieving its employment and inflation goals are roughly in balance.

for_you.text: On a $5,000 card balance at about 21.76% APR, a 25 bp cut lowers monthly interest by about $1.04.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 4.31% and moved -11 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 6.72% would fall by about $21.86 a month.
High-yield savings rates usually follow the Fed partly; on $10,000 that means roughly $15.00 a year less in interest.
Unemployment was 4.1%, and employers added an average of 66k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 2.6% over the past year (October 2024); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 2.9%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 3.2% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -6 bp on the day, and the S&P 500 moved 0.74%.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.74% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that future rate adjustments will depend on incoming data, the evolving economic outlook, and the balance of risks.
